name: Midtrans
why_it_matters: GoTo Group-owned gateway named by Kontan (Sep 2025) as one of Indonesia's three main payment gateways; its docs list 16+ methods: BCA/BNI/BRI/Permata virtual accounts, Mandiri Bill Payment, GoPay, ShopeePay, QRIS, Indomaret/Alfamart, Akulaku and Kredivo. No public share figure found.

name: Xendit
why_it_matters: Indonesia and Philippines gateway named by Kontan (Sep 2025) among the three main Indonesian gateways; its product page lists virtual accounts (BCA, BRI, Mandiri), QRIS, OVO/DANA/ShopeePay, retail outlets (Alfamart, Indomaret, 12,000+ stores) and cards. No public share figure found.

name: DOKU
why_it_matters: Self-described pioneer gateway, Bank Indonesia PJP Level 1 licence; 45+ methods (cards, BCA/BNI/BRI/Mandiri banks, Alfamart/Indomaret/Lawson cash, OVO/DANA/LinkAja/QRIS, Akulaku/Kredivo PayLater); claims 150K+ merchants and 360M+ transactions. Adyen routes Indonesian bank transfer and convenience-store payments through DOKU.

name: BCA
why_it_matters: Largest private bank and card acquirer; its 2026 e-commerce acquiring product sheet offers two gateways (BCA Payment Gateway and Mastercard Payment Gateway Services). Bank Indonesia data cited by Kompas (2020) put BCA at 23% of the payments industry and 26% of credit cards.

name: Bank Mandiri
why_it_matters: State-owned bank; Mandiri Bill Payment virtual account is on every domestic gateway (Midtrans, Xendit, DOKU). Bank Indonesia data cited by Kompas (2020) put Mandiri at 16% of the payments industry; no current acquiring share figure found.

name: Antom
why_it_matters: Ant International aggregator; its docs list for Indonesia DANA, GoPay, LinkAja, OVO, ShopeePay, BCA online banking, ATM Bersama/Prima/Alto, BNI, CIMB Niaga VA, Maybank and Kredivo BNPL, plus global cards. No public share figure found.

name: Adyen
why_it_matters: Offers DANA and GoPay directly plus Indonesian bank transfers (ATM, mobile, online banking) and convenience-store cash via partner DOKU; its Indonesia guide notes card penetration below 20%. No local acquiring statement found for Indonesia.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Indonesia docs list cards (Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Amex), virtual accounts, cash (Alfamart), OVO recurring, DANA, LinkAja, ShopeePay and QRIS. No public share figure found.

name: QRIS
why_it_matters: Bank Indonesia's national QR standard: 59 million users, 13.66 billion transactions and 42 million merchants in 2025 (BI, Jan 2026); 2026 target 17 billion transactions. Worldpay GPR 2026 says BI-FAST and QRIS lead online payments in Indonesia.
typical_access: via Midtrans, Xendit, DOKU, dLocal, Rapyd

name: Bank transfer / virtual accounts (BCA, Mandiri, BNI, BRI, Permata)
why_it_matters: Bank transfer took 27% of e-commerce value (PPRO, 2022 data), second only to wallets; virtual accounts from BCA, Mandiri, BNI, BRI and Permata are standard on every gateway.
typical_access: via Midtrans, Xendit, DOKU, dLocal, Antom, Adyen (DOKU), Airwallex

name: ShopeePay
why_it_matters: Ipsos survey (Feb 2026) found ShopeePay used by 91% of respondents in the past three months, the highest of any Indonesian wallet, with 41% top-of-mind awareness. Wallets were 39% of e-commerce value (PPRO).
typical_access: via Antom, Airwallex, dLocal, Xendit, Midtrans

name: GoPay
why_it_matters: GoTo's wallet; Ipsos (Feb 2026) found 67% of respondents used it in the past three months; PPRO cites a 10% e-commerce share; Adyen says it is accepted by 900,000+ merchants. Worldpay GPR 2026 names GoPay, DANA and OVO as the leading wallets.
typical_access: via Midtrans, Antom, Adyen, Airwallex, 2C2P, Boku

name: DANA
why_it_matters: Ant-backed wallet; Ipsos (Feb 2026) found 67% of respondents used it in the past three months; Adyen cites over 30 million users. Named by Worldpay GPR 2026 among the three leading Indonesian wallets.
typical_access: via Antom, Adyen, Checkout.com, Airwallex, dLocal, Xendit, DOKU, 2C2P, Rapyd

name: OVO
why_it_matters: Grab-affiliated wallet; Ipsos (Feb 2026) found 44% of respondents used it in the past three months, fourth behind ShopeePay, GoPay and DANA; named by Worldpay GPR 2026 among the leading wallets.
typical_access: via Antom, Airwallex, dLocal, Xendit, DOKU, 2C2P, Rapyd, PPRO

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards were only 17% of e-commerce value (PPRO), split Visa 48%, Mastercard 36%, local schemes 3% (GPN is the domestic scheme); Adyen notes card penetration below 20%. Bank installment plans are offered via 2C2P IPP with Maybank, CIMB, BCA and OCBC NISP.
typical_access: direct via BCA or Mandiri acquiring, or via Adyen, dLocal, 2C2P, Antom, Midtrans, Xendit

name: Alfamart / Indomaret (convenience-store cash)
why_it_matters: Cash was 11% of e-commerce value (PPRO); Indomaret and Alfamart over-the-counter payment is offered by every domestic gateway (Midtrans, Xendit, DOKU) and by dLocal and Airwallex.
typical_access: via Midtrans, Xendit, DOKU, dLocal, Airwallex, Adyen (DOKU), PPRO

name: Kredivo / Akulaku (BNPL)
why_it_matters: ResearchAndMarkets (Feb 2025) sizes Indonesia BNPL at about US$8.59 billion for 2025 and describes Akulaku and Kredivo as the domestic leaders; Bank Indonesia data cited by Kontan show PayLater use up 32.18% year on year to March 2025.

name: Razer Merchant Services
why_it_matters: Razer Fintech's B2B arm (formerly MOLPay); described as the first online acquirer in Malaysia to enable Discover acceptance; RMS Online supports 110+ payment methods and Razer Fintech reported US$7 billion TPV in FY2021.

name: iPay88
why_it_matters: One of Malaysia's oldest gateways (founded 2006); supports 37+ payment channels and recurring payments per HitPay's comparison. No public share figure found.

name: eGHL
why_it_matters: Online payment arm of GHL Systems; operates in 5 countries, supports 100+ payment channels and 48 currencies, with instalment options. No public share figure found.

name: Maybank
why_it_matters: Malaysia's largest bank, listed first among GlobalData's key players in Malaysian cards and payments (2026); appears as an FPX bank on dLocal and as an IPP instalment bank on 2C2P. No public acquiring share figure found.

name: CIMB
why_it_matters: GlobalData key player (2026); CIMB Clicks is named by PPRO as a popular bank-transfer app and CIMB is an IPP instalment bank on 2C2P. No public acquiring share figure found.

name: Public Bank
why_it_matters: GlobalData key player (2026); FPX bank on dLocal and IPP instalment bank on 2C2P. No public acquiring share figure found.

name: Adyen
why_it_matters: Launched local acquiring in Malaysia in 2020; its guide says online banking is 50% of Adyen's Malaysian volume and credit-card penetration is 20%. Own pages confirm FPX, DuitNow, Boost, GrabPay and Atome for Malaysia.

name: Stripe
why_it_matters: Stripe accounts in Malaysia can accept FPX (PayNet-owned, nearly 90 million transactions in 2018 per BNM) and GrabPay (MYR). No local acquiring statement found.

name: Antom
why_it_matters: Docs list Boost, GrabPay MY, Touch 'n Go eWallet, ShopeePay and FPX for Malaysia; Touch 'n Go is reached through Alipay+. No public share figure found.

name: FPX (online banking)
why_it_matters: Bank transfer was the top e-commerce method at 37% of value (PPRO, 2023); FPX is owned by PayNet (BNM plus 11 banks) and Adyen says online banking is half its Malaysian volume.
typical_access: via Stripe, Adyen, Antom, Airwallex, dLocal, Razer Merchant Services, iPay88, eGHL, PPRO

name: DuitNow QR / DuitNow Transfer
why_it_matters: DuitNow QR volume more than doubled to 3 billion transactions in 2025 (BNM figures via Fintech News Malaysia); PayNet reports more than 3 million registered DuitNow QR touchpoints and 8.44 billion total transactions in 2025. Worldpay GPR 2026 forecasts A2A at 40% of Malaysian online value by 2030.

name: Touch 'n Go eWallet
why_it_matters: Ipsos (Dec 2025) found 78% of Malaysian e-wallet users used Touch 'n Go in the past three months, far ahead of MAE (44%) and ShopeePay (10%); wallets were 26% of e-commerce value in 2025 (Worldpay GPR 2026).
typical_access: via Antom (Alipay+), Checkout.com, Airwallex, dLocal, 2C2P, Boku, PPRO

name: GrabPay
why_it_matters: Grab's wallet; Ipsos (Dec 2025) found 4% past-three-month usage in Malaysia, behind Touch 'n Go, MAE, ShopeePay and Setel; Adyen cites around 38 million monthly Grab users across the region. Named by Worldpay GPR 2026 among Malaysia's leading wallets.
typical_access: via Stripe, Adyen, Antom, Airwallex, dLocal, 2C2P, Boku, PPRO

name: Boost
why_it_matters: Axiata-backed wallet named by PPRO and Worldpay GPR 2026 among Malaysia's leading wallets; no public share figure found.
typical_access: via Adyen, Antom, Airwallex, dLocal, 2C2P, PPRO

name: ShopeePay
why_it_matters: Ipsos (Dec 2025) ranked ShopeePay third among Malaysian wallets at 10% past-three-month usage; named by Worldpay GPR 2026 among the leading wallets.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards were 28% of e-commerce value (PPRO, 2023); Adyen puts credit-card penetration at 20%; MyDebit is the domestic debit scheme (GlobalData). Bank instalment plans are available via 2C2P IPP with Maybank, CIMB, Public Bank, RHB, Hong Leong, AmBank, Affin, OCBC and HSBC.
typical_access: direct via Maybank, CIMB or Public Bank, or via Adyen (local acquiring), Stripe, Razer Merchant Services, 2C2P, Antom, dLocal

name: Atome / SPayLater (BNPL)
why_it_matters: Atome is available for Malaysia and Singapore on Adyen (MYR settlement requires a Malaysian entity) and on Airwallex; SPayLater is listed by Airwallex for Malaysia. No public share figure found.

name: 7-Eleven (cash)
why_it_matters: Cash was 6% of e-commerce value (PPRO, 2023); 7-Eleven Malaysia over-the-counter payment is listed by Airwallex and dLocal.

name: Maya Business
why_it_matters: Merchant arm of the Maya wallet (50 million users in 2022 per Gulf News); offers Checkout, QR Ph, POS terminals and Apple Pay acceptance, acting as wallet-as-acquirer. No public merchant share figure found.

name: PayMongo
why_it_matters: Philippine gateway stating it is built on the platform behind 350,000+ businesses and US$18B+ in payments in the Philippines; HitPay's comparison lists GCash, Maya, QR Ph, GrabPay, ShopeePay, SPayLater and BillEase on it.

name: Xendit
why_it_matters: Philippines coverage includes online banking, GCash and Maya wallets, over-the-counter (7-Eleven, Cebuana, Palawan Express, M Lhuillier) and cards. No public share figure found.

name: Dragonpay
why_it_matters: Online-banking and over-the-counter aggregator listed as a Philippine bank-transfer method by Airwallex and PPRO, and exposed by Adyen as a convenience-store variant. No public share figure found.

name: BDO
why_it_matters: BDO describes itself as the largest card acquirer in the industry, accepting all BancNet ATM/debit cards and major card brands; listed by GlobalData (2025) as the first key player. No public acquiring share figure found.

name: BPI (Global Payments JV)
why_it_matters: BPI's merchant acquiring (POS and e-commerce) runs through its joint venture with Global Payments formed in 2015 (Global Payments 51%); merchants are referred to Global Payments. BPI online banking is also a payment method on Antom and dLocal.

name: Antom
why_it_matters: Docs list GCash, Maya, GrabPay PH, ShopeePay, BPI and UnionBank online banking and BillEase BNPL for the Philippines; GCash is reached through Alipay+. No public share figure found.

name: Adyen
why_it_matters: Offers GCash (PHP processing, USD settlement) and GrabPay for the Philippines (online only); its guide notes card penetration among Southeast Asia's lowest. No local acquiring statement found.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Lists cards, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Maya and GCash wallets, cash at Cebuana, LBC, Palawan Express and M Lhuillier, and UnionBank/BPI bank transfers. No public share figure found.

name: GCash
why_it_matters: Mynt's IPO filing reports 39.1 million monthly active users and PHP 17.0 trillion payments GTV for 2025, from 90 million registered users; Worldpay GPR 2026 puts wallets at 41% of e-commerce value in 2025 with GCash first.
typical_access: via Antom (Alipay+), Adyen, Checkout.com, Airwallex, Xendit, PayMongo, Maya Business, dLocal, 2C2P, Boku, PPRO

name: Maya
why_it_matters: Second wallet; Maya Wallet reached 50 million users in 2022 (Gulf News, Sep 2024) and is named by Worldpay GPR 2026 among the leading Philippine wallets. No 2025 user figure found.
typical_access: via Antom, Xendit, PayMongo, dLocal, 2C2P, Maya Business

name: QR Ph / InstaPay (online banking)
why_it_matters: BSP: QR Ph processed 2.47 billion transactions worth PHP 1.16 trillion in 2025 and for the first time exceeded debit and credit card transactions; digital payments reached 64.7% of retail volume. Worldpay GPR 2026 puts A2A at 13% of e-commerce value in 2025.
typical_access: via Maya Business, PayMongo, Antom (BPI, UnionBank), Airwallex (Philippines Online Banking), dLocal, Xendit, Dragonpay

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards were 30% of e-commerce value (PPRO), but Adyen notes card penetration among the lowest in Southeast Asia; bank instalments via 2C2P IPP with HSBC, Metrobank, BDO and RCBC.
typical_access: direct via BDO or BPI-Global Payments, or via Adyen, 2C2P, Antom, dLocal, Xendit, PayMongo

name: Over-the-counter cash (7-Eleven, Cebuana, M Lhuillier, LBC)
why_it_matters: Cash was 15% of e-commerce value (PPRO) and Worldpay GPR 2026 puts cash at 42% of in-store value in 2025; OTC networks are offered by Xendit (7-Eleven, Cebuana, Palawan, M Lhuillier), dLocal and Dragonpay.
typical_access: via Xendit, dLocal, Dragonpay (Dragonpay OTC also via Adyen)

name: Cash on delivery
why_it_matters: Worldpay GPR 2026 puts COD at 23% of Philippine e-commerce value in 2025, one of the highest in the region.

name: GrabPay
why_it_matters: Listed for the Philippines by Adyen (online only), Antom, dLocal and 2C2P; no public Philippine share figure found.

name: ShopeePay / SPayLater
why_it_matters: Named by Worldpay GPR 2026 among the leading Philippine wallets; Airwallex lists both ShopeePay and SPayLater for Philippine shoppers. No public share figure found.

name: BillEase (BNPL)
why_it_matters: ResearchAndMarkets (Mar 2025) sizes Philippine BNPL at about US$3.21 billion for 2025 and profiles BillEase first among providers; Antom lists BillEase as its Philippine BNPL method.

name: DBS
why_it_matters: Largest local bank; e-commerce card acceptance through certified gateways (Mastercard Payment Gateway Services, eNETS) with PayLah! checkout and next-working-day settlement; listed as a Visa acquirer in Singapore.

name: UOB
why_it_matters: Listed by Visa as a Singapore acquirer; merchant services cover Mastercard, JCB, UnionPay and Visa with 3DS online acceptance and multi-currency processing. No public acquiring share figure found.

name: OCBC
why_it_matters: Listed by Visa as a Singapore acquirer alongside DBS and UOB. No public acquiring share figure found.

name: NETS
why_it_matters: Domestic debit network and eNETS online gateway; listed by Visa as a Singapore acquirer and supported as a certified gateway by DBS; Adyen names NETS payments among Singapore methods.

name: Adyen
why_it_matters: Holds a direct Visa/Mastercard acquiring licence in Singapore; own pages confirm PayNow (SGD), GrabPay and Atome. Its guide cites 7.7 million cards in circulation and 55% of transactions cross-border.

name: Stripe
why_it_matters: Singapore accounts can accept PayNow (real-time) and GrabPay (SGD) in addition to cards incl. JCB and UnionPay; listed by Visa as a Singapore acquirer.

name: Airwallex
why_it_matters: Listed by Visa as a Singapore acquirer; docs list PayNow, GrabPay, Atome, ShopeePay and SPayLater for Singapore shoppers.

name: Worldpay
why_it_matters: Listed by Visa as a Singapore acquirer (WorldPay Pte. Ltd.); Worldpay states it offers domestic acquiring in nine Asia-Pacific markets (2025).

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards led e-commerce at 44% of value (US$10.8B) in 2025 (Worldpay GPR 2026; PPRO showed 53% earlier); JCB and UnionPay are accepted via 2C2P and Checkout.com (JCB beta); bank instalments via 2C2P IPP with UOB, DBS, OCBC, HSBC, SCB and Amex.
typical_access: direct via DBS, UOB or OCBC, or via Adyen (local licence), Stripe, Checkout.com, Worldpay, Airwallex, 2C2P

name: PayNow
why_it_matters: MAS/ABS (Jun 2026): about 11 million proxy registrations covering over 90% of adults and 350,000 businesses; SGD 154 billion in consumer payments in 2025 across 23 banks and 6 PSPs. Worldpay GPR 2026 forecasts A2A at 13% of e-commerce value by 2030.
typical_access: via Stripe, Adyen, Airwallex, Rapyd, Checkout.com (beta)

name: GrabPay
why_it_matters: Wallets took 40% of e-commerce value (US$10B) in 2025 with GrabPay named first (Worldpay GPR 2026); PPRO also names GrabPay as the leading local wallet.
typical_access: via Stripe, Adyen, Antom, Airwallex, 2C2P, Boku, PPRO

name: Apple Pay / Google Pay
why_it_matters: Worldpay GPR 2026 and PPRO name Apple Pay (and Samsung Pay) among Singapore's popular wallets on top of the 44% card base; no separate share figure found.
typical_access: via any card acquirer (Adyen, Stripe, Checkout.com, DBS)

name: ShopeePay
why_it_matters: Named by Worldpay GPR 2026 among Singapore's leading wallets after GrabPay; listed for Singapore by Antom and Airwallex. No public share figure found.

name: Atome (BNPL)
why_it_matters: Singapore-headquartered BNPL available on Adyen (SGD, USD settlement) and Airwallex for Singapore; no public share figure found.

name: NETS / eNETS
why_it_matters: Domestic debit scheme; Adyen names NETS payments among Singapore methods and DBS supports eNETS as a certified e-commerce gateway. No public e-commerce share figure found.

name: 2C2P
why_it_matters: Bangkok-rooted regional PSP (Alipay+/Antom-affiliated): 400+ payment options, 600,000+ over-the-counter points across Asia, cards incl. JCB and UnionPay, LINE Pay, and bank instalments (IPP) with SCB, Bangkok Bank, KTC, KBank, TBank, Citi and Krungsri.

name: Omise
why_it_matters: Thai gateway that returned to the Omise name in 2025 after operating as Opn; 2025 newsroom shows QR PromptPay and streaming-payment partnerships and an AI payments launch (Nov 2025). No public share figure found.

name: Kasikornbank (KBank)
why_it_matters: One of the five biggest Thai banks Adyen connects for online banking; IPP instalment bank on 2C2P; its K PLUS banking app is a payment method on Antom. GlobalData lists it among key players (2025). No public acquiring share figure found.

name: Siam Commercial Bank (SCB)
why_it_matters: Among the five banks Adyen connects for Thai online banking and an IPP instalment bank on 2C2P; GlobalData key player (2025). No public acquiring share figure found.

name: Bangkok Bank
why_it_matters: Among the five banks Adyen connects for Thai online banking and an IPP instalment bank on 2C2P; GlobalData key player (2025). No public acquiring share figure found.

name: Krungsri (Bank of Ayudhya)
why_it_matters: Krungsri Payment Gateway accepts Visa, Mastercard and JCB with 13 settlement currencies; requires a Krungsri account, THB 2 million share capital and a THB 200,000 guarantee deposit. No public acquiring share figure found.

name: Adyen
why_it_matters: Connects five Thai banks (SCB, KTB, Bangkok Bank, Krungsri, KBank) for online banking with THB processing; its guide says 35% of online purchases are paid by COD or at convenience stores and credit-card penetration is around 8%.

name: Worldpay
why_it_matters: Launched domestic merchant acquiring in Thailand in July 2025 with LINE Pay, TrueMoney, PromptPay and online banking alongside cards.

name: Antom
why_it_matters: Docs list TrueMoney (via Alipay+), LINE Pay, K PLUS, ShopeePay and online banking with Bangkok Bank, Krungsri, GSB, KBank, KTB and SCB for Thailand. No public share figure found.

name: PromptPay / Thai QR
why_it_matters: Worldpay GPR 2026: PromptPay drove 44% of online spend in 2025; Stripe's guide cites nearly 80 million registrations (Jan 2025) and 2.1 billion transactions worth THB 4.43 trillion in March 2025 alone.
typical_access: via Stripe, Airwallex, Worldpay, dLocal, Rapyd, Omise, 2C2P, PPRO

name: Online banking / bank transfer (SCB, KBank, Bangkok Bank, Krungsri, KTB)
why_it_matters: Bank transfer was the top e-commerce method at 42% of value (PPRO); Adyen and Antom both connect the five largest banks directly.
typical_access: via Adyen, Antom, Airwallex (Thailand Online Banking), 2C2P, Worldpay, dLocal

name: TrueMoney
why_it_matters: Leading Thai wallet: Bangkok Post reports 27 million users of which 17 million active; named first by Worldpay GPR 2026 and PPRO. Wallets were 25% of e-commerce value (PPRO).
typical_access: via Antom (Alipay+), Checkout.com, Airwallex, Worldpay, dLocal, Boku, PPRO

name: Rabbit LINE Pay
why_it_matters: Airwallex describes it as one of the top two e-wallets in Thailand (THB, max THB 49,999 per transaction for Thai users); named by Worldpay GPR 2026 among the leading wallets. No public share figure found.
typical_access: via Airwallex, Antom (LINE Pay), 2C2P, Worldpay, dLocal

name: ShopeePay
why_it_matters: Fintech News (Jan 2026) cites over 30 million users in Thailand (via siampay.com); named by Worldpay GPR 2026 among the leading wallets.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards were 21% of e-commerce value (PPRO), split Visa 63%, Mastercard 25%, local schemes 11% (Thai Payment Network); Adyen puts credit-card penetration around 8%. Bank instalments via 2C2P IPP with SCB, Bangkok Bank, KTC, KBank, TBank, Citi and Krungsri.
typical_access: direct via KBank, SCB, Bangkok Bank or Krungsri gateways, or via Worldpay (domestic acquiring), 2C2P, Omise, Adyen, Stripe, dLocal

name: Cash / over-the-counter (Tesco Lotus, Big C, 7-Eleven) and COD
why_it_matters: Adyen: 35% of online purchases are paid via cash on delivery or at convenience stores; Worldpay GPR 2026 says Thailand's COD share of e-commerce is among the highest globally. Cash was 10% of e-commerce value (PPRO).
typical_access: via Airwallex (Tesco Lotus), dLocal (Tesco Lotus, Big C), 2C2P (OTC network)

name: BNPL (Atome, K PAY LATER, SPayLater)
why_it_matters: ResearchAndMarkets (Feb 2025) sizes Thai BNPL at about US$3.94 billion for 2025 and names Atome, K PAY LATER, SPayLater and Pay Next as dominant providers.

name: NAPAS
why_it_matters: National payment switch and domestic card scheme; its online gateway lets e-commerce merchants accept domestic cards and accounts from 40 member banks with tokenised two-factor authentication; NAPAS volume grew 24% in 2025 while ATM withdrawals fell 29%.
typical_access: direct (via member bank or licensed intermediary)

name: VNPay
why_it_matters: Payment gateway and QR network with the widest coverage, over 350,000 acceptance points (Vietstock, 2024); Decision Lab gave its wallet 16% share in 2023. Listed as a wallet on dLocal.

name: Payoo
why_it_matters: Vietnamese payment intermediary named by Visa (Jun 2025) among the acquirers and payment facilitators launching Click to Pay, alongside Alepay, Sacombank and VietinBank. No public share figure found.

name: Alepay
why_it_matters: Vietnamese online gateway named by Visa (Jun 2025) among the acquirers and payment facilitators launching Click to Pay. No public share figure found.

name: Vietcombank
why_it_matters: GlobalData (2025) lists Vietcombank among Vietnam's key card players; it is a NAPAS member and appears in dLocal's bank-transfer list. No current public acquiring share figure found.

name: Techcombank
why_it_matters: NAPAS (Nov 2025) names Techcombank a leader in promoting NAPAS 247 instant transfers; a pioneer issuer of Visa Click to Pay (2025) and a GlobalData key player. No public acquiring share figure found.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Lists cards incl. NAPAS, wallets MoMo, VNPay, VTPay and Ninepay, and bank transfers across 20+ banks incl. Vietcombank, Techcombank and VietQR. No public share figure found.

name: Antom
why_it_matters: Docs list MoMo, Viettel Money and ZaloPay wallets for Vietnam plus global cards. No public share figure found.

name: Adyen
why_it_matters: MoMo is in Adyen's payment-method index; its Vietnam guide says cards take 31% of online payments with NAPAS the main debit card and COD at 26%. No local acquiring statement found.

name: VietQR / NAPAS 247 bank transfer
why_it_matters: NAPAS: VietQR transactions up more than 52% in volume and 85% in value in the first ten months of 2025, with nearly 90 million mobile-banking accounts scanning VietQR; bank transfer was 21% of e-commerce value (PPRO).

name: MoMo
why_it_matters: Decision Lab (2023) gave MoMo 68% wallet market share with about 31 million users; the company claims over 40 million active users as of late 2025. Wallets were 31% of e-commerce value (PPRO) and Worldpay GPR 2026 forecasts 38% by 2030.

name: ZaloPay
why_it_matters: Second wallet: Decision Lab (2023) gave it 53% share and 14 million users; VNG's 2025 annual report (via Digital in Asia) puts active users at 20 million by mid-2025 with volume up 82%.

name: NAPAS domestic cards
why_it_matters: Local schemes account for 87% of Vietnam's card mix (PPRO) and Adyen calls NAPAS the main debit card; NAPAS's gateway covers domestic cards from 40 member banks.
typical_access: via dLocal (Napas), NAPAS gateway, PPRO (local cards)

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards were 27% of e-commerce value (PPRO) and 31% per Adyen, but international schemes are only Visa 7% and Mastercard 6% of the card mix; Visa launched Click to Pay with Techcombank and VPBank in June 2025.
typical_access: direct via Vietcombank, Techcombank, Sacombank or VietinBank, or via dLocal, Antom, Adyen, 2C2P, Payoo, Alepay

name: Cash on delivery
why_it_matters: Worldpay GPR 2026 puts COD at 16% of Vietnamese e-commerce spending in 2025; PPRO shows cash at 18% of e-commerce value and names COD a popular method.

name: ShopeePay / SPayLater
why_it_matters: Decision Lab (2023) gave ShopeePay 25% wallet share; named by Worldpay GPR 2026 among the leading wallets; the only Vietnam methods on Airwallex are ShopeePay and SPayLater.

name: BNPL (Fundiin, Atome, Kredivo)
why_it_matters: ResearchAndMarkets (Feb 2025) names Fundiin, MoMo, Atome and Kredivo as leading Vietnamese BNPL providers in a market projected at US$8.5 billion by 2030. No provider share figures found.

name: MPU (Myanmar Payment Union)
why_it_matters: National payment network and domestic card scheme; launched its e-commerce service on 13 Feb 2015 (with 2C2P as technical provider) and reports 600+ e-commerce merchants, 905,000+ registered e-commerce members and 158,000+ daily transactions.
typical_access: direct (via MPU member bank) or via 2C2P

name: 2C2P
why_it_matters: The only cross-border aggregator in this set listing Myanmar: Visa, Mastercard and MPU cards; it built MPU's e-commerce platform in 2015. Antom, Adyen, Stripe, Airwallex, dLocal and Rapyd list no Myanmar methods.

name: KBZ Bank
why_it_matters: Largest private bank and operator of KBZPay, which offers businesses a centralised payment gateway and API; Fintech News (Nov 2023) cites 160,000 confirmed merchants on its business app and about 910,000 total merchants.

name: Wave Money
why_it_matters: First licensed mobile financial services provider (2016, Telenor/Yoma JV); GSMA cited by The Fintech Times put it at around 80% of the mobile financial services market; its app listing cites about 60,000 agents and 200,000+ merchants with instant merchant payment.

name: CB Bank (CB Pay)
why_it_matters: Named by The Fintech Times (Jun 2026) among the banks whose wallets (CB Pay) shape Myanmar's digital payments; no public figures found.

name: AYA Bank (AYA Pay)
why_it_matters: Named by The Fintech Times (Jun 2026) among the banks whose wallets (AYA Pay) shape Myanmar's digital payments; AYA also issues MPU-JCB co-branded cards. No public figures found.

name: KBZPay
why_it_matters: Huawei case study: more than 22 million users (nearly 60% of adults) and annual transactions up from 2.1 billion in 2024 to over 3.8 billion in 2025 (vendor-reported). Fintech News reported 19 million active users (43% of adults) for 2024.
typical_access: direct (KBZPay merchant gateway); not listed by any aggregator reviewed

name: WavePay (Wave Money)
why_it_matters: Leading mobile financial service by agent reach (about 60,000 agents, 200,000+ merchants per its app listing; GSMA put Wave at around 80% of the MFS market); cash shortages after 2021 pushed consumers toward wallets.
typical_access: direct; not listed by any aggregator reviewed

name: MPU cards
why_it_matters: Domestic debit/credit scheme; MPU reports 905,000+ registered e-commerce members and 600+ online merchants; co-branded with JCB and UnionPay for international use.
typical_access: via 2C2P, or direct via MPU member banks

name: Cards
why_it_matters: 2C2P lists Visa and Mastercard acceptance for Myanmar, but The Fintech Times (Jun 2026) notes sanctions and international de-risking limit access to global payment networks, with EU sanctions extended until at least May 2027 and the World Bank projecting a 2.5% GDP contraction in FY2025/26.
typical_access: via 2C2P, or direct via KBZ, CB or AYA Bank

name: AYA Pay / CB Pay
why_it_matters: Bank wallets named by The Fintech Times (Jun 2026) alongside KBZPay, Wave Money and OnePay as the main wallet developments; no public user figures found.
typical_access: direct; not listed by any aggregator reviewed
